dayLines: You push through the doors into open air. Haven grounds — tents, a fire pit, worn paths. The world is that way.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 1 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
You break ground behind the hall — bed 2 of 2, turned and ready. Sow seed to start a crop.
💧 A person, maybe 50s, with sun-creased eyes returns with water: +4 clean.
💧 A woman, maybe 30s, with calloused knuckles returns with water: +3 clean.
💧 A woman, maybe 50s returns with water: +2 clean.
📨 Word came: a lean teacher wants to join Haven. "I saw you on the broadcast. You looked like people who eat." — they haven't set foot here. The village will judge.
📓 Journal: a lean teacher applied remotely.

"Hey." A woman, maybe 30s, with calloused knuckles settles near you, not too close. "Day one. Everyone's pretending they're fine. ...Can we talk? Just talk — like people used to." (Talk to A woman, maybe 30s, with calloused knuckles.)
Recipe: Bark armor (Level 1). You have seen bark armor. Plates of bark laced together, worn like a shell.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
A cold snap. Breath smokes. The woods go quiet.
⚠ STARVING: health and energy falling. You went to bed on an empty stomach.
Village meal: +1200 kcal, +1L water from the communal pantry. (Half ration — they don't trust you yet.)
A man, maybe 20s is staring into the fire like it owes them answers.
A woman, maybe 30s, with calloused knuckles is hurt — a fall, a thorn, a bad step. (health 81/100)
Tanya and Raj lingered over the fire together.
You remember the Fire-hardened spear at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
You remember the Flannel Shirt at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
— DAY 2 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
👀 the woman in her 30s, with a crooked nose says to belong somewhere is the dream. Funny how the dream never comes up when they're the one choosing what to do with an afternoon.
📓 Journal: jotted down what they said (A woman, maybe 30s, with a crooked nose).
Snow by morning. (0°C — Cold) The ground goes iron — forage thin, walking dear.
Diana Carranza reads the sky: clear tomorrow, cold.
A person, maybe 40s, with deep-set eyes will work the garden once each day while at Haven. Other orders take priority.
You step into the Haven hall.
📋 A person, maybe 40s, with restless hands — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
A person, maybe 40s, with deep-set eyes doesn't say a word. They just stand there, arms crossed, until you finish giving the order. The silence does the talking.
📋 A person, maybe 40s, with deep-set eyes — 🎣 Fish. They'll report back by next part.
(Talking costs a little energy — 10 kcal a conversation. Small talk is cheap; going deep costs time, not more food.)
Hunger gnaws. The pack is thin — work the green, haul it back, get it named at camp. That's the whole game.
...and then it lands: A woman, maybe 50s speaks 🇮🇳 Hindi. You share no language at all.
They point at themself and say it slowly, twice. It sounds like a name: Fatima.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Fatima).
Fatima speaks only 🇮🇳 Hindi. No shared words at all — just eyes, hands, and patience.
"Luis," they say, touching their chest. "I'm Luis." You'll remember that.
📓 Journal: learned their name (Luis).

Open sky for the first time in a while. Hawks circle — something down there is being watched.

This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.

— Nut trees —
Hickories and oaks, heavy with mast. This is a pantry that grows.
Movement — a big brown bat cutting arcs through the dusk.
👁 It hears you coming mid-wingbeat — in the air, you don't catch it. Hunt it roosting at dawn, or wait for the water it must come down to.
This patch is worked out — step to another green patch and forage again.

Travel 2 tiles to creek.
— Moving water —
The water is cold enough to hurt your teeth. Downstream the creek bends out of sight, and you want to follow it. That's the problem with creeks.
Something moves out there — a drumbeat with no drummer, getting closer.
✅ You saw the creek. A woman, maybe 20s nods. "Good. Now we know." (+integration)
Unfamiliar unknown roots — into the bag. (Unknowns lump together; sort them at camp.)
📓 Journal: you UNDERSTAND **Green Thumb, Literally**. It resonates with: something unnamed, something unnamed.
A shot in the dark — you take what's green: 3× unknown roots. Into the bag, unnamed. (Not food until identified — sort them at camp.) This patch is picked clean — it'll recover in a few days.
Travel 1 tile to Haven.
The drumbeat with no drummer stops at the treeline — pacing, unwilling. The walls end the argument. It's still out there.
1 unprocessed haul onto the counter — the clock is ticking.
Someone by the fire nods at the counter. "We pool food here. Keep what you need for the road — the rest feeds everyone, once it's food."
Nobody at the fire knows your haul any better than you do. It'll be your own hands that teach you.
You walk back into Haven. 3 Codex entries. The village is glad to see you.

A man, maybe 20s has been asking about the strange leaves all week — "but what IS it?" Tonight, an answer. Fireside lesson: Diana passes around a tall grass with a dense bottle-brush grain head. Someone asks a dumb question. Nobody minds. That's how you learn.
★ IDENTIFIED: Pearl Millet. Tall grass, dense grain head like a bottle brush. This is food. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
You were listening. Now you know Pearl Millet too.

Fatima spends the afternoon with the giant rhubarb-like leaves, round burrs, first-year = leaf rosette with no stalk — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. An hour passes. Then another. Nothing. The fire nods. That's dinner, maybe.
From the lumped bag: Burdock — named, and out.

Fatima: "It offered me something. A... gift? I said no. I don't trust gifts from the sky."
